sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Dumbbell Lateral Raise is an isolation exercise that targets the lateral (side) head of the deltoid muscle.

It is one of the most effective exercises for building wider, more defined shoulders and creating that sought-after capped shoulder look.

This movement is a staple in shoulder training programmes for all experience levels.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Builds shoulder width and definition
- Isolates the lateral deltoid effectively
- Improves shoulder stability and joint health
- Creates a balanced and proportional upper body appearance
- Enhances overhead pressing strength
- Low equipment requirement — just a pair of dumbbells
- Easy to adjust intensity by changing weight or tempo

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Lateral Deltoid (Side Shoulder)

Secondary: Anterior Deltoid, Supraspinatus, Upper Trapezius, Serratus Anterior

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Stand with your back straight, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing inward).
3. Arms fully extended by your sides, palms facing your body.
4. Keep your elbows slightly bent (soft lock).
5. Chest up, shoulders back, core braced.
6. Maintain a slight forward lean at the torso (5-10 degrees).

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Keeping your torso stationary, lift the dumbbells out to your sides.
2. Raise your arms in a smooth arc until they reach shoulder level.
3. Keep your elbows slightly bent throughout the movement.
4. Lead with your elbows, not your hands — think of pouring water from a jug.
5. Hold for a count of one at the top while squeezing your shoulder muscles.
6. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
7. Do not swing or use momentum — keep the movement strict.
8. Repeat for the desired number of reps.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Using too much weight and swinging the body for momentum
- Lifting the dumbbells too high (above shoulder level), engaging the traps excessively
- Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
- Fully locking out the elbows, placing stress on the joint
- Rushing the eccentric (lowering) phase
- Leaning too far back during the lift
- Not maintaining a slight bend in the elbows throughout

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Pair of Dumbbells (light to moderate weight)
- Optional: Resistance Band (for added tension at the top)
- Optional: Lifting Gloves (for grip comfort)
- Recommended: Mirror (to check form)

sections.heading: Weight Selection
sections.content:
1. Start lighter than you think — the lateral raise is a strict isolation exercise.
2. Beginners: 2-5 kg (5-10 lbs) per hand.
3. Intermediate: 5-10 kg (10-20 lbs) per hand.
4. Advanced: 10-15 kg (20-30 lbs) per hand.
5. Form should never be sacrificed for heavier weight.
6. If you need to swing or shrug to lift the weight, it's too heavy.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Feet shoulder-width apart, stable base.
2. Grip: Neutral grip, palms facing your body.
3. Elbows: Slight bend maintained throughout.
4. Shoulders: Depressed (pulled down away from ears).
5. Torso: Slight forward lean, chest up.
6. Core: Braced to prevent swinging.
7. Head: Neutral position, eyes forward.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Cable Lateral Raise: Constant tension from the cable
- Machine Lateral Raise: Guided movement path
- Behind-the-Back Cable Lateral Raise: Different resistance angle
- Plate Front Raise: Targets anterior deltoid
- Barbell Upright Row: Compound shoulder width builder
- Band Lateral Raise: Progressive resistance

sections.heading: Lateral Raise Variations
sections.content:
Seated Lateral Raise: Eliminates momentum and lower body involvement
Incline Lateral Raise: Lying on an incline bench for constant tension
Lean-Away Lateral Raise: Hold a post and lean away to increase range
21s Lateral Raise: 7 partial bottom, 7 partial top, 7 full reps
Pause Lateral Raise: Pause at the top for 2-3 seconds
Drop Set: Start heavy and immediately reduce weight when you fail

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Shoulder Pain: Try cable lateral raises with lighter weight, or machine variant
Wrist Discomfort: Adjust grip angle or use a thumbs-up grip
Neck/Trap Tension: Focus on depressing shoulders before and during the lift
No Dumbbells: Use resistance bands, cables, or water bottles
Mobility Issues: Reduce range of motion and gradually increase
Learning Stage: Use very light weight, perform slow controlled reps in front of a mirror
